- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.7), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.  
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is negative, model is likely overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model’s 30-day average, adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +1, –1, +1), model often fails to capture volatility; apply ±2% correction based on last sentiment direction.
